name: Impairment of Unique Digital Assets
title: Impairment of Unique Digital Assets
answer: Impairment of unique digital assets covers the accounting question of when a non-fungible token, a unique on-chain collectible, or a similar one-of-a-kind digital holding has lost value and must be written down. It sits inside digital asset accounting, alongside questions of how such assets are recognised, measured and disclosed. The topic matters because unique tokens rarely have a quoted market price, so the usual fair value evidence is thin. It also touches tax and reporting, since a write-down can change the carrying amount shown in financial statements.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Impairment of unique digital assets covers the accounting question of when a non-fungible token, a unique on-chain collectible, or a similar one-of-a-kind digital holding has lost value and must be written down. It sits inside digital asset accounting, alongside questions of how such assets are recognised, measured and disclosed. The topic matters because unique tokens rarely have a quoted market price, so the usual fair value evidence is thin. It also touches tax and reporting, since a write-down can change the carrying amount shown in financial statements.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on the same ledgers and accounting systems that hold the rest of the books, extended with a register of token identifiers, wallet addresses and acquisition costs. On-chain data from public blockchains supplies ownership and transfer history, and marketplace records supply whatever sale prices exist. Valuation inputs often come from third-party pricing services, appraisers or auction results, and these are held in spreadsheets or valuation models. Controls over wallet keys and over who can change a carrying amount sit on top of that stack.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Practitioners first establish the unit of account, meaning the specific token rather than a class of tokens, because uniqueness is the whole point. They then test for indicators of impairment, such as a fall in the floor price of a comparable collection, a failed sale, or the loss of the platform that gave the asset utility. Where an active market exists, the measurement uses observable prices, and where it does not, the measurement falls back on models, appraisals or the most recent arm's length transaction. The write-down is recorded, the new carrying amount is carried forward, and the reasoning is documented for the auditor.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk turn on custody, because a token held by a third party or in a compromised wallet raises questions about control and about who bears the loss. Provenance matters as well, since the acquisition record, the mint history and the chain of transfers support both the cost basis and the ownership claim. Accounting frameworks differ on whether unique digital assets are treated as intangibles, inventory or something else, and that classification drives whether impairment is tested and how reversals are handled.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward clearer measurement guidance for assets that have no comparable, and toward better pricing data as marketplaces and index providers mature. More automation is likely, with on-chain data feeding impairment tests directly rather than through manual spreadsheets. Expect continued debate over whether unique digital assets belong in existing intangible asset rules or need their own category.
